paragraphs.heading: A long warm spell
paragraphs.text: The Holocene Climate Optimum was a warm stretch in the first half of the Holocene epoch, lasting roughly from 9,500 to 5,500 years before present. Its warmest point came around 8,000 years ago. It goes by many other names, including the Altithermal, the Hypsithermal and the Mid-Holocene Warm Period. Afterward temperatures slid slowly downward, by about 0.1 to 0.3 °C every thousand years, until about two centuries ago. Shorter regional warm spells rode on top of that long decline.

paragraphs.heading: How warm it got
paragraphs.text: Compared with the Last Glacial Maximum, the optimum was about 4.9 °C warmer. A 2020 study looked at its warmest 200 years, around 6,500 years ago, and put the global average about 0.7 °C above the nineteenth-century mean, just before the Industrial Revolution. The same study put that peak 0.3 °C below the 2011–2019 average. The 2021 IPCC report said, with medium confidence, that the last decade has been warmer than this period.

paragraphs.heading: Uneven warmth
paragraphs.text: The warmth was not spread evenly over the globe. Simulations show Northern Hemisphere summers warmer than today's average, while the tropics and parts of the Southern Hemisphere ran colder than average. The size of the change fell off sharply with latitude, so low and middle latitudes show essentially no shift in mean temperature. Tropical reefs mostly show rises of less than 1 °C, yet Svalbard, near the North Pole, was about 6 °C warmer than now. Even within Europe, the northwest warmed while the south cooled.

paragraphs.heading: A warmer Arctic
paragraphs.text: In the western Arctic, 120 of 140 studied sites show clear signs of conditions warmer than today. At 16 sites with numerical estimates, local temperatures averaged 1.6±0.8 °C higher than now. The Arctic had less sea ice, and the Greenland Ice Sheet thinned, most of all at its edges. Northwestern North America warmed first, between 11,000 and 9,000 years ago, while the Laurentide Ice Sheet still kept eastern Canada cold. Northeastern North America reached its peak 4,000 years later.

paragraphs.heading: Monsoon rains reach inland
paragraphs.text: In Asia, rising seas and shrinking ice sheets in the Northern Hemisphere let the rain belt of the East Asian Summer Monsoon spread northwest, deep into the continent's interior. That monsoon was at its strongest during this interval and much weaker before and after it. With more rain, parts of what is now desert in Central Asia were widely covered in forest. In the Yarlung Tsangpo valley of southern Tibet, rain and snow reached up to twice today's amounts.

paragraphs.heading: Forests, farms and savannas
paragraphs.text: In the Middle East, the optimum brought frost-free winters and plentiful Pistacia savannas. It was during this time that cereals were domesticated there and Neolithic populations grew. In China, the steady climate of the middle Holocene helped farming and animal herding take hold. In the southwestern Iberian Peninsula, forests reached their greatest extent between 9,760 and 7,360 years ago, thanks to ample moisture and warm temperatures.
